subject.title: [Bug] Missing connection recovery state machine in gateway websocket client

question: Should the generic Gateway client ever buffer and replay requests across a disconnected socket, or must callers continue receiving immediate failures and explicitly retry replay-safe work?
rationale: Reconnect scheduling already exists, while transparent buffering creates ordering, duplication, cancellation, and stale-request semantics that source inspection alone cannot define safely.

options.title: Keep explicit retry
options.body: Retain immediate request failure on disconnect and repair only a reproducible reconnect-state defect, leaving replay decisions to callers that know whether an operation is safe.

options.title: Add typed replay safety
options.body: Introduce an explicit protocol or request-level replay-safe classification before buffering only operations whose duplication and ordering contracts are defined.

options.title: Buffer all requests
options.body: Queue every request during reconnect, accepting the compatibility and duplicate-operation risks of delayed transparent replay.

recommendation.title: Keep explicit retry
recommendation.body: Retain immediate request failure on disconnect and repair only a reproducible reconnect-state defect, leaving replay decisions to callers that know whether an operation is safe.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision affects the shared Gateway client and protocol contract, for which this is the strongest feature-history routing signal.
